title: the butter thief
carry: two trees fall, two men go free

segments.voice: Yesterday the butter thief let himself be tied, once he saw how tired his mother was. Your line was he lets himself be tied.
screen: `THE BUTTER THIEF.` · `HE LETS HIMSELF BE TIED.`

segments.voice: So there he is, a small boy roped to a heavy wooden mortar, and his mother has gone back to her housework. A child might sulk, or cry. Krishna looks around the yard. Near the house stand two tall arjuna trees, side by side. And the Bhagavata lets us in on something nobody in the village knows: those two trees used to be people. They've been standing there a long time, waiting for this exact boy. Today the mortar goes for a walk.
screen: `TIED TO THE MORTAR.` → `TWO ARJUNA TREES.` → `THEY USED TO BE PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: The trees were once Nalakuvara and Manigriva, the sons of Kubera, the god of wealth. Proud and drunk, they were playing in a river with a crowd of young women, wearing nothing, when the sage Narada happened by. The women, embarrassed, covered themselves at once. The brothers didn't bother. So Narada cursed them to stand as trees, but his curse came with a way out: they would stand until they saw Krishna, and then be free. A curse, in this telling, that was also a kindness, because what they lacked was humility, and a tree has time to learn it. Now Krishna crawls toward them, dragging the mortar. He squeezes between the trunks. The mortar turns sideways and wedges against them. He pulls, and with a great crack both trees come crashing down. Out step two shining figures. They bow to the child, praise him, ask that their speech, eyes and hands be given to him from now on, and leave. The cowherds come running at the noise. Who did this? The children playing nearby say: Krishna, dragging the mortar. The grown-ups can hardly believe it. Nanda unties his son, smiling. Look back at this week. A baby carried across a flooding river at night. Putana, blessed in spite of herself. A village that can't stay angry at a thief. And a punishment, a boy tied to a mortar, that becomes the way two prisoners go free.
screen: `KUBERA'S SONS, PROUD AND DRUNK.` · `NARADA'S CURSE, WITH A WAY OUT.` · `THE MORTAR WEDGES BETWEEN THEM.` · then, large: `TWO TREES FALL, TWO MEN GO FREE.`

segments.voice: Feel the weight of your body resting down, like something rooted, and bring to mind one thing that has felt like being tied in place lately: a wait, a limit, a delay you didn't choose. Breathe with it and ask quietly whether anything is being freed, or learned, because you're stuck here, and let the question rest if no answer comes. If you pray, you can hold that place in your prayer.
Nalakuvara. One of two proud, drunk sons of Kubera, cursed to stand as trees until they saw Krishna and were set free.
Your line: two trees fall, two men go free. Tomorrow, a mother looks into a small mouth. That's a week, done.

screen: `DAY 889 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE MOUTH FULL OF UNIVERSE.`

howItsDone: The freeing of Kubera's sons, called Yamalarjuna in Sanskrit, the twin arjuna trees, is retold in Krishna devotion as part of the Damodara story, and some images show the child pulling the mortar between two trees.
